title: Kim2025 – 40-class beta-range SSVEP speller dataset
description: A 40-class steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface speller dataset acquired from 40 healthy subjects using beta-range stimulation frequencies (14.0–21.8 Hz) to reduce visual fatigue. The dataset comprises 33-channel EEG recordings (31 scalp + 2 mastoid references) sampled at 1024 Hz during a 5-second SSVEP stimulation task, with 6 sessions per subject and 6 trials per class, totaling 240 trials per participant. This derivative dataset was processed using the Mother of All BCI Benchmarks (MOABB) framework and is designed to support the development and benchmarking of SSVEP-BCI classification algorithms.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 40 healthy subjects (25 males, 15 females, aged 20–35 years) using a BioSemi ActiveTwo amplifier with 31 active scalp electrodes plus 2 mastoid reference electrodes in a standard 10-05 montage. Stimuli were presented as a 5×8 matrix of visual flickers on a 120 Hz monitor using the joint frequency-phase modulation (JFPM) approach with phase differences of 0.5π between adjacent stimuli. Each trial consisted of 1.5 s rest, 0.5 s cue, and 5.0 s SSVEP stimulation. EEG was sampled at 1024 Hz and stored as epochs spanning [−2000, 5000] ms relative to stimulus onset, with the event marker placed at stimulus onset (sample 2048). Subjects completed 6 blocks of 40 trials each across 6 sessions.
